title: Depression pay: 35 cents a night at open-air dances
summary: Bergen says he never made money; in the Depression he played open-air dances near Spanish Fort for as little as 35 cents a night, meeting Charlie Storr there.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: I came from Rome, this big Roman.
Well this is the second row of money. We were talking about money, how much money you made.
Oh come on, I've never made money in my life. I got all the gifts except the gift of making money.
But I mean, this is depression.

Oh yeah, we were playing at the Dharma Dance. It wasn't a prevelle, it was open air. I lived the second Spanish Forge, which location is now the Old Beach. Sometime we would make 35 cents a night. A fella named Ingehorn used to play with us out there. He was just starting with his metal clarinet. Charlie Storr, I met him out there. That's where I met Charlie, he'd sit in with us. Charlie Storr? Yeah, Starrer Storr.
